name: step-tracker
title: Step Tracker
description: Progress through a multi-step flow: the line fills on a spring, steps take a check and the new one sends a ring.

perf.budget: Plain views: one shared value for the line and three per step, changed only when the step changes. Nothing runs at rest.

a11y.reducedMotion: The line, the checks and the current step change at once, without the ring.
a11y.screenReader: Each step reads its label, its place and its status ("Payment, step 3 of 4, current step"). Finished steps are buttons when onStepPress is set.
a11y.touchTarget: Each step's column is the target, at least 44 pt tall and a share of the width.

meta.guide:
## Usage

```tsx
import { StepTracker } from '@/components/kinetik/step-tracker';

<StepTracker
  steps={['Cart', 'Address', 'Payment', 'Review']}
  current={step}
  onStepPress={setStep}
/>;
```

`current` is the index of the step in progress. Set it to `steps.length` when the flow is finished and every step shows a check.

## When to use

- Checkout, sign-up and setup flows with three to five steps.
- Any flow where knowing how much is left keeps people going.

## When not to use

- More than five steps, or long labels. Show "Step 3 of 8" with a progress bar instead.
- Flows whose steps can be done in any order. Use a checklist.

## Notes

- Steps share the width equally, so keep labels to a word or two.
- With `onStepPress`, finished steps become buttons that go back. Steps ahead never respond.
- A step changes a moment after the line starts to move, so the eye follows the fill to it.
- With reduced motion everything changes at once.

docs: Prefer `npx kinetik-ui add step-tracker`: it installs dependencies with expo install, so versions match your Expo SDK.
